name: Stift Wilten
kurzbeschreibung: Historic Wilten Abbey in Innsbruck impresses as a spiritual centre with sumptuous baroque architecture, monastery traditions, and the famed Wilten Boys' Choir.
beschreibung:
Overview

The venerable Wilten Abbey (Stift Wilten) at the southern gateway to Innsbruck is North Tyrol's oldest active monastery, with a heritage spanning nearly a millennium. Founded around 1138 by Bishop Reginbert of Brixen, this Premonstratensian canonry has been continuously inhabited and sustained by its religious community ever since. Following destruction in preceding centuries, the present sumptuous baroque abbey complex was erected during the 17th and 18th centuries by distinguished Tyrolean architects, including Christoph Gumpp. The monastery is renowned not only for its precious artistic collections and the mythical founding tale of the giant Haymon, but also as the historic home and training centre for the world-famous Wilten Boys' Choir (Wiltener Sängerknaben), one of the oldest choral traditions in Europe.

Route & Requirements

The expansive monastery grounds, featuring the magnificent collegiate church, courtyard, and prelates' gardens, are easily accessible on flat, step-free stone paths. A thorough tour of the sanctuary, the historic entrance hall showcasing monumental statues of giants Haymon and Thyrsus, and the abbey museum takes about an hour. The visit involves no physical difficulty and is perfectly suited for cultural enthusiasts, senior travellers, and families with pushchairs. While the church is accessible during liturgical services, the private cloister areas remain reserved for monastic life.

Visiting & Getting There

Wilten Abbey enjoys superb public transit links from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof and the historic old town. Tram lines 1 and 6, as well as the Stubaitalbahn (STB), stop right outside the monastery gates at the 'Stift Wilten' station. Motorists will find public parking spaces throughout the Wilten district. The abbey church is open daily throughout the year with complimentary admission. The abbey museum, with its treasury of medieval relics, baroque paintings, and illuminated manuscripts, is accessible via guided tours.

Tips

Pause at the church portal to view the imposing statues of the mythical giants Haymon and Thyrsus, legendary figures tied to the founding of the abbey. Directly across the road stands the exquisite Wilten Basilica (Basilika Unserer Lieben Frau unter den vier Säulen), a rococo architectural jewel well worth combining with your visit. Music aficionados should check the liturgical calendar in advance to experience the acclaimed Wilten Boys' Choir performing during festive Sunday high masses.
